sources.title: N. Johnson and D. Yau, 2-Dimensional Categories (arXiv:2002.06055)
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §2.1: Definition 2.1.3 (printed pp.25-27), Example 2.1.26 (printed pp.32-33); Chapter 4 §4.1: Definition 4.1.2 and Explanation 4.1.5 (printed pp.103-105); Chapter 6 §6.2: Definition 6.2.8 and Explanation 6.2.9 (printed pp.182-183), §6.3: Lemmas 6.3.2, 6.3.4 and Example 6.3.6 (printed pp.185-187); Chapter 7 §7.4: Theorem 7.4.1 (printed pp.215-216)

contents.name: Definition 2.1.3: bicategory data (objects, hom categories, identity 1-cells, horizontal composition) with the unity and pentagon axioms
Definition 4.1.2 and Explanation 4.1.5: lax functors, unitary and strictly unitary functors, pseudofunctors (invertible laxity constraints), strict functors, local equivalences
Definition 6.2.8 and Explanation 6.2.9: biequivalence via mutually inverse pseudofunctors and internal equivalences
Theorem 7.4.1 (Whitehead Theorem for Bicategories): a pseudofunctor is a biequivalence iff it is essentially surjective on objects, essentially full on 1-cells and fully faithful on 2-cells
Example 2.1.19: monoidal categories are one-object bicategories

Example 2.1.26 (Bimodules): the bicategory Bimod with rings as objects, bimodules as 1-cells, bimodule homomorphisms as 2-cells, tensor products as composition, and the associator/unitors of tensor products
Lemma 6.3.2 (Dual Basis I): M is projective iff it admits a dual basis, and finitely generated projective iff the indexing set can be finite
Lemma 6.3.4 (Dual Basis II): for a right R-module M the coevaluation K tensor_R Hom_R(M,R) -> Hom_R(M,K) is an isomorphism for all K iff M is finitely generated and projective
Example 6.3.6 (Duality for modules): an (S,R)-bimodule M is a left adjoint in Bimod iff M is finitely generated and projective over R, and then Hom_R(M,R) is its right adjoint
Chapters 8-12 (bicategorical Yoneda, coherence, tricategories, double categories, Bimod as horizontal bicategory of a double category)
contents.reason: These developments concern the general theory of 2-dimensional categories; the Morita pair needs only the bicategory axioms, pseudofunctors, biequivalence and the Bimod instance, and importing Yoneda or coherence machinery would add pages without supporting any claim of this pair.

sources.title: W. Crawley-Boevey, Noncommutative Algebra (Bielefeld lecture notes, 2016/17)
sources.locator: §1.4 Algebras (printed p.3, centre Z(R)); §3.12 Morita Equivalence (printed pp.67-69, including the Definitions, the reconstruction Theorem, the Morita Theorem and Examples (i)-(ii))

contents.name: Section 1.4: the centre Z(R) = {r in R : rs = sr for all s}

Section 3.12 Definitions: cocomplete abelian category; P finitely generated iff Hom(P,-) preserves coproducts; P a generator iff every M admits an epimorphism P^(I) -> M; R is a projective generator of R-Mod
Section 3.12 Theorem: an abelian category A is equivalent to R-Mod iff A is cocomplete and has a finitely generated projective generator P with R = End(P)^op
Section 3.12 proof: F = Hom(P,-) is faithful, then full, then dense using a presentation R^(I) -> R^(J) -> M -> 0 and the cokernel in A
Section 3.12 Theorem (Morita): R-Mod and S-Mod are equivalent iff some S-R-bimodule M gives an equivalence by M tensor_R -, iff S = End_R(P)^op for a finitely generated projective generator P
Section 3.12 Examples (i): R is Morita equivalent to M_n(R); the module R^n is a finitely generated projective generator with End_R(R^n)^op = M_n(R)
Section 3.12 Examples (ii): if e in R is idempotent and ReR = R then R is Morita equivalent to eRe, via the multiplication map Re tensor_{eRe} eR -> R and End_R(Re)^op = eRe

Section 3.12 closing applications: semisimple artinian rings are products of matrix rings over division rings and are Morita equivalent to products of division rings; deformed preprojective algebras and reflection functors as Morita equivalences
contents.reason: These are representation-theoretic applications of the Morita classification to quivers and semisimple rings; this pair builds the ring-theoretic equivalence theory and the matrix-ring witness only, and the applications would need quiver and decomposition material from other pages.

sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Chapter 1 §1.8 (author final version)
sources.locator: §1.8 (printed pp.8-11): Definitions 1.8.1-1.8.6, the paragraph after Definition 1.8.6 on projective generators and A = End(P)^op (printed p.10), Remark 1.8.7, Propositions 1.8.15, 1.8.17

contents.name: Definition 1.8.5: a finite k-linear abelian category is one equivalent to A-mod for a finite dimensional algebra A, which is determined only up to Morita equivalence
contents.reason: The intrinsic finite-category notion and its module realization are the subject of the HA-27 pair finite-abelian-categories-and-eilenberg-watts, which proves the finite-dimensional reconstruction from a finite projective generator.

contents.name: Definition 1.8.6: the intrinsic finite conditions (finite dimensional Hom spaces, finite length, enough projectives, finitely many simples)
contents.reason: The four intrinsic finite conditions and their equivalence with A-mod are proved on the HA-27 page together with the finite projective generator construction, and are not needed for the general small-projective-generator theorem here.

contents.name: Paragraph after Definition 1.8.6: A = End(P)^op for a projective generator P, and F = Hom_C(P,-) is exact when P is projective and faithful when P is a generator

Paragraph after Definition 1.8.6: conversely every exact faithful functor from a finite category to finite dimensional vector spaces is represented by a unique projective generator up to unique isomorphism
Remark 1.8.7: the dual of a finite abelian category is finite, via A-mod <-> A^op-mod and the dual module
contents.reason: Duality for finite abelian categories belongs to the finite-category pair, where the dual module functor and projective covers and injective hulls are developed; the general reconstruction here uses no duality.

contents.name: Proposition 1.8.17 (Gabber): a locally finite abelian category with an object whose finite direct sums cover every object as a subquotient has a projective generator, hence is finite
contents.reason: Gabber's criterion is a sufficient condition for finiteness and is proved in the finite-category pair; the present pair assumes the small projective generator rather than deriving it from a covering object.

contents.name: Propositions 1.8.10-1.8.15: endomorphism algebras of exact functors, tensor products of exact functors, and End(F1) tensor End(F2) = End(F1 tensor F2)
contents.reason: Endomorphism algebras and tensor products of exact functors over finite categories are used by the Deligne-product pair, which classifies bilinear right exact functors and their kernels.

sources.title: nLab, Morita equivalence (wiki entry, revision of the page consulted 2026-10-05)
sources.locator: Idea; Classical Morita theorem; Definitions (in algebra) and the following lemma and list of Morita invariants; later sections inspected for scope only

contents.name: Idea: Morita equivalence as equivalence in the 2-category of rings with bimodules as 1-morphisms and bimodule homomorphisms as 2-morphisms, related by Eilenberg-Watts to linear equivalences of module categories
Classical Morita theorem: equivalence of module categories, existence of inverse bimodules with an adjoint equivalence, and R = End of a finitely generated projective generator are equivalent
Definitions (in algebra): the center of an algebra is isomorphic to the center of its category of modules and Morita equivalent algebras have isomorphic centers
Lemma following the classical theorem: M is a left adjoint in Alg_k iff M is finitely generated projective as an S-module (proved through Cauchy completion and enriched profunctors)
Definitions in homotopy theory, Lie groupoid theory and tensor category theory (Morita morphisms, differentiable stacks, categorical Morita equivalence of tensor categories)
contents.reason: These are different Morita notions for homotopy theories, Lie groupoids and tensor categories; this pair treats rings and their module categories, while the tensor-category variant is a separate development in the representation-theory track.

contents.name: Other Morita invariant ring properties: simple, semisimple, left or right Noetherian, left or right Artinian
contents.reason: These invariance statements need the corresponding ring-theoretic classes and their module-theoretic characterisations, none of which occur in this pair's items; the pair records only the center invariant, which its own proof establishes.

sources.title: J. Fuchs, G. Schaumann, C. Schweigert, Eilenberg-Watts calculus for finite categories and a bimodule Radford S^4 theorem (arXiv:1612.04561v3)
sources.locator: Introduction (printed pp.1-3), including the classical statement, formulas (1.1)-(1.4) and the Lex/Rex triangle; §§2.1-2.2, 3.1-3.2 and 3.5-3.6 inspected for scope and deferred to the finite-category, Deligne-product and graded pairs

contents.name: Introduction: classical Eilenberg-Watts theorem for unital rings (right exact plus coproduct preserving equals tensoring with an S-R-bimodule) and its Morita-invariant reformulation
Introduction (1.1)-(1.4) with Proposition 2.8: B box A^op is the category of B-A-bimodules, and the regular and coregular bimodules are expressed as end and coend of m box m*
contents.reason: The Deligne product identification and the end and coend formulas for the regular and coregular bimodules are constructed in the Deligne-products pair, which proves the finite Deligne product and kernel calculus.

contents.name: Introduction triangle A^op box B <-> Lex(A,B) <-> Rex(A,B): left exact and right exact functors for finite linear categories are both classified by the opposite Deligne product
contents.reason: The Lex and Rex classification for finite linear categories is the main theorem of the finite-category pair; the present pair treats arbitrary rings and all bimodules and does not need finiteness.

contents.name: Sections 3.5-3.6: the end/coend formulas for kernels, the Nakayama functors, and the bimodule Radford S^4 theorem
contents.reason: Nakayama functors and the Radford S^4 theorem are proved in the Deligne-products pair through its explicit kernel end and coend calculus; they are not used by the Morita bicategory statements.

contents.name: Sections 2.1-2.2 and 3.1-3.2: finite end/coend inverse calculus and the adjoint triangles for finite categories
contents.reason: The finite end and coend inverse calculus and the adjoint triangles for finite linear categories precede the Deligne-product classification on its own page; the general reconstruction here uses copowers and cokernels instead.
